title: Relay operability: metrics, usage events, verse-advertised relays, TLS/backup/self-host docs
description: Make the headless relay (fe-relay) and the GUI's own API surface operable by a self-hoster and consumable by a downstream operator: opt-in OpenMetrics /metrics (separate bind, off by default), a UsageEvent + UsageSink trait emitted from fe-api middleware (no-op default, JSON-lines file sink as the reference impl), structured JSON logs, a SurrealKV backup/restore runbook, a self-hosted iroh-relay recipe (FE_SYNC_RELAY) so operators are not pinned to n0's rate-limited public fleet, a documented reverse-proxy TLS recipe (rustls opt-in deferred), a consolidated env-var config reference, and a new S-RELAY-ADVERTISE seam: relays advertised in a verse's own doc (a new __relays table, Owner/Manager-gated) are added/removed at runtime via iroh 1.3's Endpoint::insert_relay/remove_relay, with a local adopt/pin/deny policy. Purely operator-facing — this is what any self-hoster needs to run and trust their own relay.
alignment: Open-core rule (conductor/open-core.md): anything a self-hoster needs to run, verify or extend FractalEngine belongs here. This track is the public owner of seams S-RELAY and S-RELAY-ADVERTISE (conductor/open-core.md Seams table), which any downstream operator tooling may consume; this repo never depends on or names such consumers. Builds on fe-sync's iroh 1.3 port (iroh_1_0_upgrade_20260711) and its §relay-health RelayConfig/RelayHealth model.
related: iroh_1_0_upgrade_20260711 (its iroh 1.3 port is landed and is what FR-7 builds on; its remaining sweep + flag-day rollout do not gate this track)
peer_networking_support_20261031 (next phase: consumes and hardens S-RELAY-ADVERTISE, adds the embedded members-only relay; its W1 waits for this track's S9 verdict)
open_decisions: OD-1 metrics bind: separate listener/port (recommended, off unless FE_API_METRICS_BIND set) vs a route on the main authenticated port
OD-2 TLS: documented reverse-proxy recipe only (recommended for v1) vs an in-process rustls listener opt-in
OD-3 UsageSink reference impl: JSON-lines file (recommended, matches the task's instruction) vs stdout-only

OD-4 self-hosted iroh-relay: a docker/compose.dev.yml service + recipe in this track (recommended); the embedded members-only iroh-relay server inside fe-relay is the next phase, peer_networking_support_20261031 FR-1/FR-3

OD-5 S-RELAY-ADVERTISE write gate: Owner/Manager role at verse scope (recommended, mirrors existing role_grants), enforced at write time and at read time on the inbound-apply path, vs self-declare-only like __peers

OD-6 S-RELAY-ADVERTISE local policy: default DialOnly (changed from AutoAdopt at the next phase's F0 review — iroh keeps one latency-chosen home relay per endpoint, so auto-inserting every advertised URL risks a members-only verse relay capturing the home slot for all verses); Pinned opts in; Deny ignores
OD-7 metrics auth: unauthenticated on its own loopback-default bind (recommended) vs reusing the Bearer JWT middleware
OD-8 /metrics content: request-count + error-count + duration histogram per route-class (recommended v1 minimum) vs also exposing P2P/sync gauges (peer count, relay health) in the same exposition
OD-9 config reference doc location: new docs/relay-operations.md (recommended) vs folding into docker/README.md only

OD-10 advertised-relay access: advertised relays never receive RelayAccessToken (insert_relay with auth_token: None; configured entry wins when a URL is in both sets); a token-gated relay must be configured, and an advertised one the peer cannot authenticate to is surfaced not adopted; admitting exactly a verse's members with no shared token is peer_networking_support_20261031 FR-3 (members-only access control keyed on the handshake-proven endpoint id)
notes: 2026-10-31: track drafted (docs only). Folded in verified findings from a peer research session on iroh 1.3: (1) hole-punching is automatic and UPnP/PCP/NAT-PMP portmapping defaults to Enabled (iroh 1.3.0 portmapper.rs, PortmapperConfig::Enabled) — the relay is the coordination/fallback channel, not something hole-punching replaces, which is why this track's observability + self-host work still matters; (2) iroh 1.3 exposes Endpoint::insert_relay/remove_relay (iroh 1.3.0 endpoint.rs) — added as the new S-RELAY-ADVERTISE seam (FR-7); (3) serving as an iroh relay needs inbound HTTPS (a public address + a TLS cert) — recorded as a non-goal (no all-peer relay mesh) with an optional future phase (embedded iroh-relay server in fe-relay); (4) leaning on data-level forwarding (gossip plumtree hops, or doc replication via any replica holder such as fe-relay) to move relay-advertisement rows or usage data widens the already-documented claim-based gossip attribution residual (fe-sync/src/AGENTS.md §transport-admission-control item 2) — recorded in Risks.

slices.task: UsageEvent struct + UsageSink trait (async) + NoopUsageSink + JsonLinesUsageSink reference impl, in fe-runtime (same crate that already hosts the transport-agnostic BlobTransport trait precedent)

fe-api usage-emit middleware (tower layer via axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state, mirrors mcp_concurrency_limit's shape): captures caller DID (from auth middleware's ApiClaims extension), MatchedPath as route class, byte counts, duration, status; ApiState/ApiConfig gain a usage_sink field + usage_sink_from_env() idiom (mirrors elevated_query_allowed_from_env/OperatorGate)

opt-in OpenMetrics /metrics on its own listener (new spawn fn, default off; bind read from FE_API_METRICS_BIND); in-memory counters fed by the same per-request hook as S2's UsageEvent (request count, error count, duration histogram per route class)
wire ApiConfig's new usage_sink + metrics_bind fields through both host binaries (env-derived, same pattern as upload_quota_bytes_from_env)
structured JSON logs: swap tracing_subscriber::fmt() for .json() behind an env toggle (FE_LOG_FORMAT=json|text, default text to avoid breaking existing operators' greppable logs) in both binaries

S-RELAY-ADVERTISE: __relays/{relay_id} doc table (ULID row: v=1, url, advertised_by, note; unknown fields ignored, unknown v skipped) + role-gated admission (Owner/Manager at verse scope, mirrors role_grants resolve_role) enforced at write time AND at read time on the inbound-apply path (quarantine; re-evaluate on advertiser demotion; SignedEntry author must equal advertised_by) + one pub fn validate_advertised_relay_url wrapping the RelayConfig URL-parsing path (the single hook peer_networking_support extends); write path reuses the generic SyncCommand::WriteRowEntry (handler at sync_thread.rs:970; its payload is a blob-store content_hash, fe-sync/src/messages.rs) — no new SyncCommand variant. Note __peers rows are NOT written through WriteRowEntry; the sync thread publishes them directly via repl.write_row(PEER_DECL_TABLE, ...) (sync_thread.rs:2051)

REST route POST/DELETE /api/v1/verses/{verse_id}/relays(/{relay_id}) — Owner/Manager role-checked (same idiom as the sim-control routes), serializes the __relays row, adds it to the blob store, and forwards its content_hash to the sync thread as WriteRowEntry

sync-thread reconciliation: watch __relays table changes (same inbound-row pump shape as PeerDeclaration/§inbound-apply), gated by a local RelayAdvertisePolicy (DialOnly default: list + dial-allowlist, no insert_relay | Deny | Pinned(urls): insert_relay with auth_token: None; env FE_SYNC_RELAY_ADVERTISE_POLICY); removal refcounted across verses; remove_relay never called on a configured URL; advertised relays never carry RelayAccessToken; an advertised token-gated relay the peer cannot use is surfaced via RelayHealth/warn!, not adopted

tripwires: metrics listener must default OFF (unset FE_API_METRICS_BIND → no second TcpListener bound at all, not just an auth-gated route)

UsageEvent must never carry node_id/asset bytes, query text or an expanded request path — caller DID + the token's scope string + route CLASS (template) + method + sizes/duration/status/timestamp only; DID and scope never become /metrics labels
S-RELAY-ADVERTISE write admission reuses fe_policy role resolution, never a new ad-hoc role check
RelayAdvertisePolicy is local-only state (never replicated) — a verse cannot force a peer to dial a relay it has denied; its default is DialOnly and only Pinned calls insert_relay
advertised relays never carry RelayAccessToken: every insert_relay from advertisement processing passes auth_token: None, and a configured entry for the same URL is left untouched
advertisement reconciliation never calls remove_relay on a configured URL (FE_SYNC_RELAY, settings, Default fleet); removal of advertised URLs is refcounted across verses
__relays admission (Owner/Manager via fe_policy) runs at read time on the inbound-apply path on every replica, not only at the REST write; the SignedEntry author must equal advertised_by

no all-peer relay mesh: in this track the self-hosted relay is a documented recipe; the embedded members-only iroh-relay server is the next phase (peer_networking_support_20261031), opt-in at build and run time, never default-on
agents never run cargo; orchestrator gates once per wave
